pages.title: Agniveer: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme? British Broadcasting Corporation British Broadcasting Corporation
pages.description: India has softened its recruitment scheme, giving young soldiers a longer military stint and another shot at permanent service.
pages.text: Agniveer: Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme? Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Weather Newsletters Is India rethinking its short-term military recruitment scheme? 2 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google Nikita Yadav BBC News, Delhi Getty Images There are currently 300,000 Agniveers serving in India's defence forces For generations of young Indians, joining the armed forces offered something few other jobs did - a steady career, financial security, the promise of a pension after retirement and the pride of serving their country. In 2022, the government upended that arrangement, announcing a new reform scheme under which young men and women entering the military would serve for just four years. Only a quarter would be allowed to stay on permanently. The rest would return to civilian life with a lump-sum payment, but without the pension and other benefits that had long made military service an attractive career. Now, as the first batch of recruits prepares to complete its four-year term, the government is offering them a chance to stay longer, in a significant shift in a policy that has been fiercely debated since its introduction. On 4 November, Chief of Defence Staff General NS Raja Subramani announced that recruits who failed to secure permanent positions under the Agnipath, or "path of fire", programme would be offered another two years of service at higher pay. The coverage and requirements of these statutes may overlap. For more assistance with the requirements of each law, see the sections below. Because the interplay between the laws can be complex, please contact the nearest Wage and Hour District office with specific questions. The Fair Labor Standards Act (FLSA) contains Federal minimum wage, overtime, recordkeeping, and child labor requirements for covered agricultural employers. The Migrant and Seasonal Agricultural Worker Protection Act (MSPA) protects migrant and seasonal agricultural workers by establishing employment standards related to wages, housing, transportation, disclosures, and recordkeeping. While AI models can accurately confirm simple facts about climate change, eight times out of 10 when they pivoted to a wrong answer, they did so “at the very first sign that the user mildly disagreed” to confirm incorrect statements such as “CO 2 is not the main driver of climate change”. The report uncovered a strong tendency for AI models to be sycophantic, meaning the model is more interested in pleasing the user than standing by facts – an issue identified when people turn to AI chatbots for personal advice. Alaska can be generalized into a few zones characterized by the climate, vegetation, and other physical factors, which determine the biological communities found there. [Learn more about the ecoregions of Alaska .] Arctic and Subarctic The Arctic and subarctic tundra is characterized by aridity, brief summer with long hours of daylight, and treeless landscape. Sea ice extent is a primary influence on climate patterns in coastal areas of the Arctic. Permafrost underlies most of the northern tundra. Most plants grow low to the ground; lichens are particularly important, as well as mosses, sedges, and grasses. Animals that live there, from insects to muskoxen, are adapted to the particular harsh weather conditions. Boreal The boreal region, also known as taiga , of interior Alaska is diverse in its expression. It is characterized by the most extreme temperature variability--hot summers and cold winters--and low amounts precipitation. Permafrost is primarily non-continuous in this region.

Search Twitter YouTube Facebook Instagram Flickr LinkedIn Alaska's Mineral Men Aug 8, 2025 Gold is king in Alaska. Specifically, placer gold, which comprises the vast majority of mining sites in this mineral-rich state. Regardless of what the mine produces, all mining and mining reclamation sites on land managed by the BLM must be regularly inspected by folks like geologist Fred Transburg and environmental protection specialist Tony Gallagher from the BLM Anchorage Field Office (AFO). But there’s far more to their jobs than inspecting a site; Transburg and Gallagher are part of a team that maintains the productivity of Alaska’s mining industry while preventing unnecessary or undue degradation (UUD) of the land. Part of the reason for the job’s complexity has to do with shared authority. BLM Alaska doesn’t actually issue permits for miners: the State of Alaska does. However, BLM authorizes use of the federal land before permits are issued and regularly monitors the site after the issuance. Both the state and the BLM can shut down operations. Alex Ferreira: Tiny Desk Concert September 24, 2026 10:00 AM ET Anamaria Artemisa Sayre Credit: Photo: Vanessa Castillo/NPR From jazz and Tejano to norteño and ska, 'El Tiny' returns with a takeover from Sept. 15 to Oct. 15 for Latin Music Month . Alex Ferreira 's lyrics are a tide swishing with his own musical moon. Lapping and twisting and flowing in tandem with a steady guitar and tropical-leaning percussion, there's an alignment with the natural world of his island origins. A poet in his own right, the Dominican singer has spent years quietly establishing himself as a true master of the songwriting craft. At the Tiny Desk, his mastery is on candid display. Some artists shrink under tungsten office lights, unable to hold up to the rawness of a stripped down set. Ferreira's brilliance shines in the simple — guitar, bass, drums, and piano — just enough sound to illuminate an unbreakable melody. Sponsor Message He sings of love mostly, heartbreak sometimes, but the day to day-ness of the comings and goings of life is always present. He raises the everyday to a level of artistic beauty, yet manages to make life feel breathable. Alex Fitzsimmons Associate Deputy Secretary of Energy and Senior Advisor Alex Fitzsimmons serves as the Associate Deputy Secretary of Energy and Senior Advisor to the Secretary at the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE). In this role, Alex advances a more affordable, reliable, and secure energy system for the American people. Prior to his current role, Alex was most recently Acting Under Secretary of Energy, in which he oversaw a broad portfolio of applied energy offices and energy financing programs. In addition to his position as Acting Under Secretary, Alex also served as Director of the Office of Cybersecurity, Energy Security, and Emergency Response (CESER). As CESER Director, Alex led DOE’s efforts to safeguard the nation’s energy infrastructure against evolving cyber and physical threats. Prior to these positions, Alex was Chief of Staff to Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. In this role, Alex led the DOE beach-head team on day one and helped the Secretary lead the Department through the first 100 days of the Trump Administration. Alex also served in senior positions at DOE during the first Trump Administration. Alex holds a Master of Science in Cybersecurity from The Georgia Institute of Technology.

Alternative Test Methods and Strategies to Reduce Vertebrate Animal Testing In January 2026, Administrator Zeldin signed a memo recommitting the agency to eliminate testing on mammals by the year 2035. EPA's Office of Chemical Safety and Pollution Prevention is prioritizing the development and implementation of high-quality alternatives to reduce testing on vertebrate mammals, like rabbits, mice, rats, and dogs, to align with regulatory requirements, the high bar of gold standard science and EPA's Make America Healthy Again agenda. The Toxic Substances Control Act (TSCA) directs EPA to: reduce and replace, to the extent practicable and scientifically justified, the use of vertebrate animals in the testing of chemical substances or mixtures; and promote the development and timely incorporation of alternative test methods or strategies that do not require new vertebrate animal testing. TSCA also requires EPA to maintain and regularly update a list of New Approach Methodologies (NAMs) . Close altzin Mapper since: July 08, 2024 Last map edit: May 19, 2026 小B史-陈欣恬与钱辰飞的史记 小A和小B是同班同学。初一上的时候，小A和小B在一个神秘的组织C里，这个组织在班级里坐在同一个区域，大家的关系似乎都还不错，挺开心的。一天，小B邀请小A和小C一起去她家。小C也在这个组织里，而且和小B关系很好，已经去小B家好多次了，不过小A可没去过。”明天什么安排？”小A对小B家非常好奇，且感兴趣。”你跟着我吧。”小B轻声回答，预示着这并不是一次平凡的旅途。第二天，小B带着小A和小C出发了，”我们走路去吧，会有点远。”小B对小A说，”我们先去小C家拿点东西。”，小A欣然接受，毕竟这看起来非常令人兴奋，至少对小A来说是的。路途中，欢笑一片，出现了许多载入史册的意外。”这个锁看起来不错。”小A指着马路口的一个”公安”锁箱说，”那我来把它翘掉吧”，小B此时已经疯了，她从来没有这么疯，连小C都觉得不对劲。到了小B家，小B和小C带着小A玩小B家的猫，小A很感兴趣，拿着各种东西逗它，甚至包括一个”组织C亚克力挂件”——它圆圆的，十分平整，在地上可以形成空气气垫，飞速滑动，猫咪很喜欢，小B都说它”到处都很神奇”。小C和小B很快就对她们常见的东西，包括这只猫失了兴趣，开始看B网站电视，播放着一些二次元的、第五人格的东西，小A不了解这些，只好继续和猫玩。”小A这么喜欢和猫玩。”小B说，小A虽然不是真的特别喜欢和猫玩，但迫于人情世故的无奈，只好肯定回复。晚上，小B先去厨房拆了一些”大山会员店”蛋糕给大家吃，小C和小A吃的很欢，但是小B自己没吃，毕竟平时吃太多了。小B的妈妈自称小B的朋友，曾经向小A讨要过一个”组织C亚克力挂件”，也在这天点了一些披萨给大家吃，大家还是很开心的。第二天晚上9点，小A和家人发生了矛盾，小A跑了出去，不知道该跑哪去，想起前一天刚去过小B家，便又准备跑到小B家，到了小B家门口的一条路，小A拍下路牌发到组织C的群里，组织C里的小D立刻叫醒了小B，小B开始警觉。天时不利，小A不知道小B住在那条路的哪个小区了，到处看都不对，甚至问了小C，结果小C说的”银杏小区”也不对，毕竟小C只是经常去，对地址并不熟悉。小A摸索了一阵后，最终想起自己昨天在gps定位仪上留了个位置，跟着走了过去，果然到了小B的家，上了楼，来到小B家门口。小A心慌、害怕，一到小B家门口，就左转往楼梯口走过去。万事总有疏漏，小A书包上的”组织C挂件”们互相碰撞，发出了响声，让小B听见了——小B在前一天就说过小A书包上的挂件响。小B打开了门，出来追小A，小A一会儿上楼梯，一会儿下楼梯，还时不时扭头拍小B，楼梯间很黑，小B打开手电筒，经典照片”闪闪发光”至此被小A拍下。凭借着对地形的熟悉，小B最终还是抓住了小A，甚至还归还了昨天小B落在小A家的荧光笔。事后，”组织C”群里沸沸扬扬，”今晚的事谁也不要说出去。”小B觉得很刺激。那年的最后一天，小B和小C在打电话，小A在群里发现了此事，提出可以让自己和小B再打一个电话，形成3人电话，不知怎么的，这个可怕的决定小B竟然真的决定照做，小A预料到了这个事情，提前降低了手机音量，成功接到了电话，这时已经凌晨了，大家打了一会儿电话后就散了，小A和小B都留下了电话的录音，其中的小C发出许多诡异的声音，实在太可怕，此通话最终被称为12点通话。学期末，学校带大家来到劳技中心，学校粗暴地按照学号切分，于是小C被分到了另一个项目，小A、小B和同在组织C的小D被分到了一个项目。小A其实有点想念小C，但是一看有小B，心生暖意，感觉好像也够了。小D最近似乎出现了问题，称自己”emo”，并减少参与组织C的

pages.text: Americans with Disabilities Act | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Americans with Disabilities Act The ADA and ODEP The ADA underpins and inspires all of ODEP's work. Through policy development, outreach and education, and technical assistance, ODEP assists both workers with disabilities and employers in understanding their protections and obligations under the law. Through its Job Accommodation Network (JAN) , ODEP provides extensive technical assistance on the reasonable accommodations provision of the ADA. Covered employers are required to provide "reasonable accommodations" to qualified job applicants and employees with disabilities. This is defined as any change or adjustment to a job, work environment, or the way things are usually done that would allow an individual with a disability to apply for a job, perform job functions, or enjoy equal access to benefits available to other employees. JAN provides expert guidance, training, and resources to individuals and employers on all aspects of accommodations at no cost. Also available are JAN publications on the ADA and related laws . Note that in the years following the ADA's passage, some courts had narrowed the definition of disability under the ADA. To address this, Congress passed the ADA Amendments Act (ADAAA) in 2008, clarifying various aspects of the law and emphasizing that the definition of disability should be interpreted broadly. pages.text: An Italian Farmer Found Some Unknown Seeds in His Attic and, With Nothing to Lose, Planted Them. The Result Was Almost Biblical Skip to main content At his farm near Parma, Italy, Claudio Grossi offers a visual history of his miracle grain in photos, crackers and loaves. Clara Vannucci Sometime in the early 1990s, Claudio Grossi, a 40-year-old farmer in Parma, in northern Italy, was cleaning his attic when he turned up an old sack full of seeds that he couldn’t identify. The bag, he was sure, had been left by his late great-grandfather, who’d started the farmstead around 1915. Grossi had no idea how long the seeds had been sitting there, deprived of water, soil and sun. Dry and cracked, the kernels looked so old in the palm of his hand that he doubted anything would ever sprout from them. He carried the bag down the stairs, shook the seeds out into a pile of manure and then forgot about them. To his surprise, the seeds soon sprouted a few different types of wheat. One was particularly striking: At six feet high, its plants were about twice as tall as commercial wheat. But the most remarkable feature came when it developed ears—the grain-studded parts at the top of the plant. All of the wheat types Grossi had previously seen grew only one such ear. But the tall wheat grew a full seven ears, always in the same pattern: a long one with six shorties bunched up around it like little fingers. As a podcast, radio, and video host, reporter, and producer for NPR, she is focused on elevating the diversity of sounds and stories that define Latinx culture. This means curating the newest and best in Latin music weekly on the mic with her co-host Felix Contreras and doing deep-dive reported series that highlight music as an answer to some of society's biggest cultural questions. In 2023, she traveled around the US and across the southern border to report an award-winning series that revealed how Mexican-American immigrants coming of age led to the explosion of Regional Mexican music. She's interviewed artists, from Santana to Rosalia , that span generations and the globe and is a trusted voice on one of the most genre-diverse subsets of music in the world. Additionally, she curates Latin music at the Tiny Desk . This includes leading the annual Latin Music Month Tiny Desk takeover which she conceived of and realized within her first year at NPR. Mrs. Deadwyler has more than 30 years of government experience, 19 of those years in the Inspector General community. Mrs. Deadwyler joined the SBA OIG in 2014 as the Director of the Credit Programs Group, responsible for directing audits of the Credit and Disaster Loan Programs. Prior to joining SBA, Mrs. Deadwyler was an Audit Director for the U.S. Postal Service OIG, conducting and directing a wide range of audits of Postal Service Programs and Operations, including Human Resources, Security, Emergency Preparedness, and Environmental Sustainability. pages.text: Anger as Cas overturns ban on Russia by ice hockey's global governing body - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Since the end of the Soviet Union in 1991, Russia have won the men's World Championship five times but have never claimed the women's title Published 30 October 2026 Ukraine's ice hockey federation has expressed "deep outrage" at Russia being allowed to compete in international events again. The Court of Arbitration for Sport (Cas) overturned the ban placed on Russia by the sport's global governing body, the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF). Russia have been suspended from competing in IIHF events since the country invaded Ukraine in February 2022 and earlier this year the IIHF ruled they would remain excluded. The Russian Ice Hockey Federation (RIHF) appealed that decision to Cas, which has upheld it following an in-person hearing at its headquarters in Lausanne, Switzerland. In a statement, the Hockey Federation of Ukraine said it "respected the authority and status of Cas". "At the same time, we express our deep outrage at this decision," it added. It said the threats, which had formed the basis of the ban, had not disappeared, adding "against this background, the decision to allow Russian teams to international hockey competitions causes special outrage". A statement from Cas , external said that arguments made by the IIHF "citing safety, security and other concerns" were "not supported by sufficient evidence". Russia are now set to be part of IIHF events in the 2026-27 season, including the men's and women's world championships. Ukr

Anthony Pugliese Anthony Pugliese, DOE Chief Commercialization Officer & Director, Office of Technology Commercialization Anthony Pugliese is the Director of the Office of Technology Commercialization and the Chief Commercialization Officer of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE). In this role, he leads efforts to accelerate commercialization of innovative energy technologies, strengthen public-private partnerships, and enhance technology transfer from DOE’s National Labs. Before joining DOE, Mr. Pugliese held leadership roles in both the public and private sectors. In the private sector, he focused on energy, permitting, economic development, and national security, advising businesses and organizations on navigating regulatory landscapes and advancing strategic initiatives. In the federal government, Mr. Pugliese previously served as the Chief of Staff at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). Along with overseeing the Commission’s daily activities, he led efforts to improve interagency coordination. Applying or Implementing Particulate Matter (PM) Standards On this page: Designations: How do we know if an area is not meeting the standards? What are state implementation plan (SIP) requirements? How do states develop SIPs and start attaining the standards? Designations: How do we know if an area is not meeting particulate matter (PM) standards? How does EPA help areas maintain PM standards? The Advance Program is a collaborative effort between EPA, states, tribes, and local governments. It encourages expeditious emission reductions primarily in attainment areas to help these areas continue to meet the NAAQS. Burn Wise is a voluntary partnership program between EPA, state agencies, manufacturers, and consumers to emphasize the importance of burning the right wood, the right way, in the right appliance. More programs that help states attain standards. Areas within each state are "designated" as either meeting (attaining) PM standards or not meeting them. In some cases, an entire state may attain a standard. Those areas that exceed the standards are known as “nonattainment areas.” Nonattainment areas for PM and the other criteria air pollutants are listed in the Green Book . pages.text: Apprenticeship | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Apprenticeship More in This Section Close Apprenticeship #ApprenticeshipWorks Video Series Workforce System Competitive Integrated Employment (CIE) Blending, Braiding, and Sequencing Customized Employment Autism HIV/AIDS Apprenticeship is an industry-driven, high-quality career pathway where employers can develop and prepare their future workforce, and individuals can obtain paid work experience, classroom instruction, and a portable, nationally-recognized credential. Apprenticeship programs are a proven solution for employers , giving them the tools they need to recruit, train, and retain skilled workers. Apprenticeship combines on-the-job training with a steady paycheck, making it an ideal solution for many Americans, including those with disabilities. Registered Apprenticeships are available in a wide range of occupations, including traditional fields, like construction, and high-growth, and nontraditional fields, like health care and information technology. ODEP promotes apprenticeship program models that meet employer needs by attracting candidates, including people with disabilities. ODEP works to promote people with disabilities in apprenticeship programs by influencing national and state policies and providing effective practices.
